title: Episode-based streams and client compact contracts (draft)
content:
Status: early draft / product brainstorming. Aim: propose a compact, ergonomic streaming contract for hosted API clients that groups related incremental output into 'episodes' (logical units), simplifies tool-calling semantics for mobile/edge clients, and provides typed checkpoints for resumability and structured extraction.

Background
- We have many docs about partial responses, typed frames, and tool handshake. This doc experiments with a slightly different mental model targeted at "small clients" (mobile SDKs, single-threaded UIs, browser tabs) and long-running agent sessions.
- Problem: clients need a small, stable contract that supports: progressive UX (partial text + structured hints), robust tool transactions (start/modify/commit/abort), resumable sessions across connectivity drops, and low implementation complexity.

Design goals
1) Compactness: minimize per-frame metadata and chattiness; fewer round-trip RPCs for common flows.
2) Grouping: let the service emit semantically grouped output ("episodes") to reduce client reconciliation work.
3) Transactional tool calls: tool interactions should be atomic from the client's perspective (optionally multi-step server-side).
4) Resumability: client can reconnect and continue seeing the latest stable checkpoint per episode.
5) SDK ergonomics: high-level client APIs should be tiny surface area: startSession(), onEpisode(), callTool(), resumeSession(), commitCheckpoint().

Non-goals
- Not solving full A/B rollout or canary behavior here (that still lives in rollout config).
- Not replacing typed streaming API for advanced desktop SDKs; this is an alternative compact surface.

User stories
- Mobile chat app shows progressive suggestions; network flakiness should not produce inconsistent state or duplicated tool calls.
- An automated assistant calls an external search tool and displays the partial answer as it arrives; if the connection drops mid-tool-run, assistant can resume status and show committed output only once tool commit is acknowledged.

Concepts
- Episode: a logical group of emission frames corresponding to a higher-level unit (e.g., an assistant reply, a tool transaction, a subtask). Episodes have stable ids (ep_*) and checkpoints.
- Frame: smallest transport unit. Types: text_delta, structured_delta, event, checkpoint, tool_invoke, tool_result, error. Frames are intentionally compact: minimal fields.
- Checkpoint: a compact stable snapshot (opaque to client) marking a durable state within an episode. Clients use checkpoints for resume and de-duplication.
- Compact contract: we favor small schemas (string-ish ids, short type tags, optional payloads) so SDKs can implement with tiny parsers.

High-level wire sketch (HTTP streaming / SSE / bidirectional websocket)
- Server sends sequence of frames, grouped by episode id. Example stream (conceptual):

[ep_start id=ep_01 meta="assistant-reply"]
[text_delta id=f1 text="We should try" ]
[text_delta id=f2 text=" this approach." ]
[checkpoint id=cp_1]
[event id=e1 type="suggested_actions" payload="[\"Refactor\", \"Explain\"]"]
[tool_invoke id=t1 tool="search" params_id=p_1]
[tool_result id=t1 result_id=tr_1 status="committed"]
[checkpoint id=cp_2]
[ep_end id=ep_01 final_summary="search-included"]

- Frames are newline delimited text lines. Each frame is a tiny JSON blob or compact key=value line depending on protocol binding. We propose two encodings: compact-text (for minimal clients) and JSON (for rich clients).

Frame fields (minimal):
- kind: text_delta | structured_delta | checkpoint | event | tool_invoke | tool_result | ep_start | ep_end | error
- ep: episode id (string)
- id: frame id (string)
- payload: opaque string (for compact binding) or JSON string for richer binding

Example compact-text binding (SSE friendly):
- Lines like: "kind:text_delta;ep:ep_01;id:f2;payload: this approach."
- Checkpoint: "kind:checkpoint;ep:ep_01;id:cp_2"

Tool transaction semantics (client-facing)
- Clients call callTool(toolName, params) -> returns a local invocation id and transitions the episode into a tool_pending state.
- Server emits tool_invoke frame referencing the invocation id (replicated to other clients).
- Server may emit interim tool_result frames with status="partial" (progress), eventually status="committed" or status="aborted".
- Idempotency: every tool_invoke has an invocation id generated by the client (or server if server-initiated). If client reconnects, replaying an invocation id is treated idempotently.
- Constraint: server guarantees at-most-once commit visibility to clients for the same invocation id (server dedup). This shifts complexity to the server but simplifies client semantics.

Resumability and checkpoints
- Checkpoints are the canonical resume markers. When reconnecting, client supplies last_seen_checkpoint id. Server streams frames starting after that checkpoint for the episode, or will send a fresh ep_start if checkpoint unknown/expired.
- Checkpoint TTL: ephemeral short-lived (e.g., 24h) for hosted-api; Dedicated/private customers may configure longer TTLs.
- Checkpoint payloads should be small (token index, output offsets) — not full model state. Server should retain mapping from checkpoint id -> deterministic replay state for resume.

Structured output patterns
- Two layered approach: lightweight schema hints + optional typed payloads.
- For many mobile apps we want to avoid big JSON parsing for every delta. Provide short event types that point to small typed payloads, e.g., event: "kb_highlight" payload_id: "p_23". Client can fetch or parse payload on demand.

SDK ergonomics (proposal)
- Surface (pseudo-API):
  - startSession(opts) -> sessionId
  - onEpisode(sessionId, callback(episode))  // episodes stream in as they start
  - episode.callTool(name, params) -> invocationId
  - episode.on('delta', cb) // text / structured deltas
  - episode.commitCheckpoint(checkpointId) - request server to pin for resume (optional)
  - resumeSession(sessionId, lastCheckpointId) -> rehydrates episodes

- High-level primitives: the SDK should expose episodes as single objects with simple lifecycle events. Clients typically only need: display deltas, show tool pending/committed statuses, and request resume.
- Backpressure and small-client constraints: SDK should buffer deltas but expose a flow-control hint: episode.requestPause() / episode.requestResume() which map to low-level TCP/websocket flow control or request-level backpressure headers.
- Automatic dedup: SDK keeps recent invocation ids (LRU) to avoid re-emitting tool calls after flaky reconnects.

Observability / telemetry
- Per-episode metrics: duration, frames_count, tool_calls, checkpoints_created, resume_count.
- Client-side: total_received_bytes, reconnects, duplicate_invocations_filtered.
- Server-side: storage duration for checkpoints, resume hit-rate, aborted_tools_ratio.

Compatibility & migration notes
- This is an alternative compact contract. Rich clients can continue to use typed streaming APIs. We'll add a translation layer inside the gateway: typed-stream -> episode frames.
- Migration plan: feature-flag on per-customer basis; start with slow rollout to mobile SDK first.

Open questions (short list)
- Should checkpoint semantics be "client-requested pin" vs automatic server checkpoints only? (pros/cons for storage cost and UX)
- What is the minimum durable info in checkpoint for resuming tools that were in-progress? (server will need to persist tool state or re-run tool idempotently)
- How to surface partial structured payloads without large JSON parsing on the main thread for mobile? (payload referencing + lazy fetch seems promising)
- Security: if payload references can be fetched by id, how do we prevent leakage across sessions? signed URLs? short-lived tokens?

Open todos
- Proto sketch (text and JSON bindings) + wire-level examples for SSE/websocket. @Jordan to draft.
- Integrations: gateway mapping to typed-streaming: implement translator that emits ep_start/ep_end and compact frames. @Luca to scope infra changes.
- SDK prototype (iOS/Android/JS): minimal episode API with resume and callTool idempotency cache. @Priya to prototype JS + mobile glue.

Notes to reviewers
- This doc favors smaller clients and simpler mental models. We intentionally offload complexity to server (e.g., de-duping tool commits). If reviewers want a server-light design, call that out.
- The episode abstraction is intentionally coarse-grained; alternative name ideas: "segment", "turn", "transactional-block".

Appendix: tiny example (JSON-rich binding)
[
  {"kind":"ep_start","ep":"ep_01","id":"es_1","meta":{"role":"assistant","purpose":"reply"}},
  {"kind":"text_delta","ep":"ep_01","id":"f1","payload":"We should try"},
  {"kind":"text_delta","ep":"ep_01","id":"f2","payload":" this approach."},
  {"kind":"checkpoint","ep":"ep_01","id":"cp_1"},
  {"kind":"tool_invoke","ep":"ep_01","id":"t1","tool":"search","payload":"{\"q\":\"how to reduce latency\"}"},
  {"kind":"tool_result","ep":"ep_01","id":"t1","status":"committed","payload":"{\"snippet\":\"use batching and kv cache\"}"},
  {"kind":"ep_end","ep":"ep_01","id":"ee_1","final_summary":"search-included"}
]

-- end draft --

Feedback welcome: quick thumbs or inline comments. Prefer short actionable items: follow-up tickets and owners.
